title: fix(spec)!: page action rows carry ActionSchema's declarative-update rules, read from one judge
body:
Fixes #23427

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

The page action rows are `action:button`, `action:icon`, and each `action:group` / `action:menu` member. They now apply `ActionSchema`'s declarative-update rules through **one judge that both read**. That closes the five members this closing card names and gives every rule in the set a verdict on the rows. Direction of record: the family's triage (`6154972534`, consistent with #23168 answer C `6148462268`) and this card's triage (`6164739115`).

## What changed

- **One judge, in one place.** `packages/spec/src/ui/action-declarative-update.ts` holds the declarative-update rules and their texts. It replaces the table and refinement that lived privately in `action.zod.ts`. `ActionSchema` calls it with its own surface, and each row calls it with the row's surface.
  - A surface is the executor key (`type` / `actionType`), whether that key defaults to `'script'`, the `onSuccess` subject, and whether `params` has a static-values object form.
  - The module is reached by relative import only, like `action-on-success-executor.ts`, and is not in the `ui` barrel.
- **`ActionSchema` is byte-identical.** A one-time corpus dump compared before and after: 152 action shapes covering every rule, every refused key, every `type`, and their combinations. Before (at `7cfc3400c`) and after the extraction, both dumps hold 572 issues with sha256 `c359828f357004883ce1b0ac4df598190839bcfdaa87898d094eb7469f54027d`, and `cmp` reports the two files byte-identical. `action-row-update.test.ts` is unchanged and green.
- **The rows** (`component.zod.ts`) run the judge first, as the runner reads `operation` first: `.superRefine(rowDeclarativeUpdate(...))` on all four rows. A row's `patch` is now `ActionSchema`'s own record, by reference (`ActionSchema.in.shape.patch.unwrap()`), the same way #23332 took `operation`.
- **Operation first.** Beside `operation: 'update'`, the rows' url-target judgment, the `'navigation'` rename and the executor half of the `onSuccess` rule stand down. The judge refuses the keys they would judge (`target`, any executor but `'script'`, `onSuccess`) whole. So a row is never told both to write `actionType: 'url'` and to drop the key. Nothing becomes accepted: each standing-down case is refused at the same key by the judge.

## H1: every rule of `ActionSchema`'s set, with its verdict on the rows

The rules are enumerated from the code (`refuseDeclarativeUpdateContradictions` and its refused-key table at `7cfc3400c`), not from the docblock.

| # | `ActionSchema` rule | where it lands | verdict on the rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `patch` without `operation: 'update'` | `patch` | **carried** on all four rows (card member 1) |
| 2 | beside the update, an executor other than `'script'` | `type` | **carried** at the row's executor key, `actionType` on a node and `type` on a member (card member 3). **Reasoned difference, text only:** a row's key has no default, so the text says the key "names that route or nothing" where the action's says "stays at its default `'script'`". An empty row key names nothing, as `effectiveRowExecutor` already reads it. A host-handler name is refused too, because the runner never dispatches it beside the update. |
| 3 | refused key `target` | `target` | **carried** (card member 2) |
| 3 | `method`, `bodyExtra`, `bodyShape` | own key | **carried** on all four rows. Not in the card's five, but in the set. |
| 3 | `recordIdField` | own key | **carried** on `action:button`. **Not applicable** on `action:icon` and members, which do not declare it, so the strict row refuses it as an unknown key. |
| 3 | `onSuccess` | `onSuccess` | **carried** since #23332, now read from the same table with the row's subject (one issue, same text as before) |
| 3 | `body`, `recordIdParam`, `outcomeMessages`, `opensInNewTab`, `newTabUrl` | own key | **not applicable**: no row declares them, so the strict row refuses each as `unrecognized_keys` before any refinement runs (pinned) |
| 4 | beside the update, nothing to write | `patch` | **carried** (card member 4). **Reasoned difference:** on `action:button` / `action:icon` a non-empty object `params` counts. On a node, `params` IS `properties.params`, the static values the renderer forwards (`readStaticParamValues`), and the runner's update merges them over `patch` (`executeUpdateOperation`). On a member an object `params` never reaches a non-`api` executor, so it does not count. |
| 5 | beside the update, a `list_toolbar` location | `locations.N` | **carried** on all four rows, which all declare `locations` (card member 5) |
| — | `objectName` (deliberately not judged in the schema; `defineStack`'s walk judges `stack.actions`) | — | **not carried**, for the action's own reason: a row acts on its own `objectName` or on the page's object, which the row cannot see. See Acceptance notes. |
| — | the `patch` key's own schema, a record | `patch` | **carried by reference**. Rule 4 reads a present `patch` as something to write, which holds only for a record. The runner drops any other `patch` before the write. |

Neighbours outside the set that read `operation`:
- The "a script action needs `body` or `target`" rule has nothing to judge on a row, because a row with no executor takes the runner's name leg.
- The `undoable` rule is not carried by any row; that is outside this family (Acceptance notes).

## H2: how the rows spell things (measured)

- **Executor.** A node spells its executor `actionType` and a member spells it `type`. A node's `type` is the component discriminator.
- **Keys the rows forward.** Every row declares and forwards `operation`, `patch`, `params`, `target`, `method`, `bodyExtra`, `bodyShape`, `locations` and `onSuccess`; `action:button` also forwards `recordIdField`. Measured at objectui's `.objectui-sha` pin `b9814b334`: the forward blocks in `action-button.tsx`, `action-icon.tsx`, `action-group.tsx` and `action-menu.tsx` (first line `type: schema.actionType` / `type: action.type`).
- **`locations`.** All four rows declare it, the same `ActionLocationSchema`.
- **What the runtimes read first.** The runner's `ActionRunner.execute` reads `operation` before any executor (`:1384-1388` at the pin, byte-identical at objectui `main` `524136e`). `executeUpdateOperation` posts through the registered `script` dispatch and merges `patch` only when it is a plain object. The platform action route treats `operation: 'update'` as the write "whatever `type` says" (`isDeclarativeUpdateAction`).

## H3: why not call `refuseDeclarativeUpdateContradictions` as-is

Its paths are relative to the refined schema, so a member's issue lands at `actions.N.KEY`. Four things still kept it from being called on a row unchanged:
- it read the executor from `type`;
- its `onSuccess` text opens with the action's subject;
- five of its texts prescribe `type: 'api'` / `type: 'script'`, which a node must spell `actionType: '…'`, because on a page component `type` is the component;
- its nothing-to-write check reads arrays only.

So the judge is extracted and parameterized. Each text is a function of the surface, and on `ActionSchema`'s surface it is the action's text byte-for-byte (proof above). The rows' pins derive the expected text from `ActionSchema`'s own parse; they do not restate it.

## H4: producer sweep (counts)

| where | hits | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `examples/**` | **0** page action rows with `patch` or `operation` | Two files carry action rows (`app-showcase` `ui/pages/index.ts`, `ui/actions/index.ts`), and neither has either key. The 6 `operation: 'update'` hits are `bulkActionDefs` and a permission set. |
| CLI corpus (`packages/cli/src/lint/corpus.ts`) | **0** | no action rows |
| dogfood fixtures (`packages/qa/dogfood`) | **0** | one ledger names the rows in prose only |
| `packages/**` test fixtures | **2 landed pins** put a non-`'script'` executor beside the update | `spec` `component-action-row-on-success-executor.test.ts`: its `BESIDE` list had `api`/`run`, giving 16 cases plus 4 "ONE TEXT" cases that read an `api` row. `lint` `validate-component-props-row-on-success.test.ts`: 2 `it.each` over 4 rows with `api`. Both now name `'script'`, and the other executors beside the update are pinned as refused in the new file. The unknown-members ledger moves `patch` to `patch{}` (`records`). |
| `skills/**`, hand-written docs | **0** | |
| objectui (read-only, after `git fetch`) | **0** spec-parsed rows | At the pin `b9814b334` and at `main` `524136e` (same list at both), 63 files mention `operation: 'update'`, and 15 of them also mention a page action row. None parses such a row against the spec; the spec reads are key-set reads and `safeParse({ size })`. One renderer test, `action-button-icon-inputs-11168.test.tsx`, mounts `{ actionType: 'script', patch: { stage: 'done' } }` (member 1's shape) at runtime as a control that nothing is written. No spec parse judges it, so no objectui test goes red at the next spec bump. objectui's own `ActionDefaultInspector` already lists the same refused keys and `list_toolbar` (`UPDATE_OPERATION_REFUSES`). |

## ADR-0087

- A new D3 entry, `18.ui-page-action-row-declarative-update-rules`; the changeset marker is `registered`, and the gate reports it new here.
- #23332's `18.ui-page-action-row-operation-declared` covers only the `operation` value and `onSuccess`, so it is not `already-registered`.
- That entry's acceptance criterion "every such row parses as before" would be false after this PR, so it now reads "… unless `ui-page-action-row-declarative-update-rules` refuses it".

## Tests

All readings come from the verify lock on a shared box. Each exit code was captured before any pipe.

**At the final head `d4f80dc9d`** (after merging `main` at `1baf976cf`):

- `@objectstack/spec` `typecheck` (tsc + scripts + test-typecheck): exit 0.
- `@objectstack/lint` unit (`vitest run --maxWorkers=2`): **139 files, 6,726 passed**, exit 0. This layer includes the props-gate door pins.
- Full build (`turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs --concurrency=2`): 75/75 tasks, exit 0.

**At `2541bab8c`** (after merging #23454's step-18 entry):
- spec unit: 677 files, 20,688 passed.
- spec typecheck: exit 0.
- lint unit: 139 files, 6,721 passed, 5 skipped.
- lint typecheck: exit 0.
- `@objectstack/cli` unit layer (`--project unit`): 284 of 287 files passed. The other three were not a reading of this diff:
  - `published-subpath-console.pin` and `published-subpath-hook-body.pin` refused because `packages/cli` itself was unbuilt (a prerequisite);
  - `hook-timeout-override-refusal` timed out twice at 5 s while spawning vitest on the loaded box.
  - After `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build`, those three files: **33/33 passed**.
- The integration layer is declared to CI.

**The new pins:** `component-action-row-declarative-update.test.ts`, every row, with code and path asserted at the parse:
- the five members, each a REFUSAL and a CONTROL;
- ONE TEXT, derived from `ActionSchema`'s own parse;
- the table's other row keys, and the undeclared keys refused as `unrecognized_keys`;
- the executor edges, `params` as the source of values, and `patch` as the action's record by identity;
- the operation-first stand-down, with a control.

Six targeted files (the new pins, #23332's pins, `action-row-update.test.ts`, the unknown-members ledger and two neighbours): **434 passed**.

## Ablation (one, on the rows' call)

On the committed tree, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `action:button`'s `superRefine(rowDeclarativeUpdate('actionType', …))` with `superRefine(() => undefined)`.
- The anchor hit once (1 → 0) and the blob changed (`54e3895c3d86` → `5f55315f502d`). The tests resolve `component.zod.ts` by relative import from `src`, so no `dist` was involved.
- **Mutated: 23 failed, 259 passed**, over the new pin file and #23332's pin file.
  - All 23 are `action:button` refusal pins: the five members, ONE TEXT, the table keys, the executor edges, `params`, the stand-down, and #23332's update pairing.
  - 0 controls and 0 other rows went red.
  - Direction: red, as predicted.
- **Restored:** the blob equals `HEAD` (`54e3895c3d86`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty, checked both by the tool and by an absolute-path trap. The same two files then ran **282 passed**.

## Gates

**Derived set.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths; the change set comes from the merge base) gives **111 families**, run at the final head `d4f80dc9d` with the tool's capture idiom.
- **All 111 exit 0.** `--ran` reconciles them as `111 derived, 111 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` (a derived zero: every family recorded an exit code).
- The run was split by an interrupted session at line 88. Lines 89-111 were re-run on the same head with the same derived list (byte-identical).
- Two families exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) in a first battery at `2541bab8c`: `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`. After the full build, both exit 0 at `d4f80dc9d`.

**Targeted spec gates.**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: all 14 artifacts up to date.
- `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main`: `registered ui-page-action-row-declarative-update-rules (new here)`.

**Stale tree, declared.** `origin/main` moved 8 commits past this head while the battery ran, with no file in this PR's surface. They changed four inputs of the derivation (`scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs`, `scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs`, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, and one `scripts/adr-anchors/` JSON). CI's runs on the merge ref are the reading for those families.

## Deviations from the claim's file surface

- **`packages/lint/src/validate-component-props-row-on-success.test.ts`** (fixture only). The dispatch fences `packages/lint/**` off; os-dev.md's fixture-triage clause requires sweeping by the rule's consumption radius.
  - Its two update pins put `api` beside `operation: 'update'`, card member 3 itself, so they would go red. They now name `'script'`.
  - No lint source changed: the props gate still reads the row schemas as they are.
- **`18.ui-page-action-row-operation-declared.ts`**: the one-clause amendment above.
- **The row `patch` by reference.** An in-place fix of the same defect class (rows accept what `ActionSchema` refuses on the declarative update), applied under os-dev's four conditions:
  - the fix is mechanical, in the #23332 shape;
  - the file is in this claim;
  - it runs under the same gate families.
  - Without it, rule 4 would accept a `patch: 'done'` row that writes nothing.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- **Released text this PR makes false.** `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` under `18.0.0-next.1` (lines 559 and 565 at `08ea7e368`) carries #23332's FROM → TO row and example `{ actionType: 'api', operation: 'update', patch: …, onSuccess: … }` → "the same row without `onSuccess` … parses unchanged". After this PR, that row is still refused at `actionType`.
  - The CHANGELOG is release-owned, so the fix is a dedicated docs-only PR amending that entry (and its consumed source, `.changeset/pre/23332-page-action-row-operation.md`).
  - This PR leaves both untouched. A merge of `main` first carried an edit into the `pre/` copy through rename detection, and `0c8c54fd8` restores it byte-identical to `main`.
- **`objectName` on a row.** No page-level walk judges an update row on a page that binds no object and names no `objectName`. Not measured as a runtime defect.
- **A page row's update on the server.** The action route looks up the DECLARED action by `name` and writes `{ ...declared patch, ...params }`, enforcing the declared param contract. So a page row's update writes only when its `name` names a registered `operation: 'update'` action on the object. Read-only inference, NOT MEASURED against a running server.
- **`recordIdField`.** objectui's `resolveServerActionRecordId` reads it when it resolves the record an update writes. The contract refuses it beside the update, and objectui's inspector mirrors that refusal, so the read is incidental, not declared.
- **`undoable` on `action:button`.** The rows carry none of `ActionSchema`'s `undoable` rule.
- **#23418.** The new entry repeats the family's "a page's `properties` is not parsed on the metadata save or load path". It is true at `main` while #23418 is open; whichever of the two lands later aligns it, as the #23332 report noted.
